last_update.summary: Censys's exposure report of 2026-10-14 points to three published 2025 AK-SM 800A flaws that Danfoss patched more than a year earlier and gives their firmware boundaries (4.3.1 or later fixes all three; Danfoss has not confirmed the vector), and shows exposed French controllers falling about 71 percent in three days with patched and unpatched builds leaving at the same rate, which Censys reads as operators taking units offline rather than patching.

last_development.summary: CERT-FR revised its alert on 2026-10-13 to add Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb to the compromised controllers, says campaigns are probably still running, and says a factory reset alone is insufficient on an unpatched end-of-life unit. NCSC Switzerland published an advisory rating the activity actively exploited and naming the current AK-SM 800A on outdated firmware, and Danfoss says that is the case for the affected current units. Blick reports that Migros uses the same Danfoss systems in a limited number of Swiss stores and sees no sign they were targeted.

records.title: Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised, with forced defrost reported at hundreds of French supermarkets; CERT-FR and NCSC Switzerland say to remove internet exposure
records.headline: CERT-FR adds Copeland and Dixell xweb to the hijacked refrigeration controllers; NCSC.ch rates the attacks exploited
records.summary: Coopérative U, Intermarché and E. Leclerc confirmed to AFP a cyberattack on their refrigeration systems overnight on 11 to 12 October 2026, which BFMTV reports as a remotely forced defrost at hundreds of stores. CERT-FR's alert, revised on 2026-10-13, reports numerous compromises of Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers and now also of Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb, says campaigns are probably still running and that a factory reset alone does not protect an unpatched end-of-life unit, and NCSC Switzerland rates the activity actively exploited. Danfoss says most affected units are legacy products or current AK-SM800A units on outdated firmware; no source names an actor, the flaw or how the attackers got in, and the Paris prosecutor is investigating.
actions: Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.

records.title: PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating
records.headline: PK Softech breach widens: Bernese cantonal funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post report the same supplier incident
records.summary: The Confederation, in a release headlined "data outflow confirmed", said on 2026-10-08 that a software supplier of Publica detected a cyberattack at the end of September, and the supplier PK Softech AG (Reinach BL) says unknown attackers used malware to reach part of its IT infrastructure and that it must be assumed data left its systems; the Federal Prosecutor's Office is investigating. Publica insures, among others, staff of the federal administration and the ETH domain, about 70,000 active members and 41,600 pensioners at the end of 2025, and its own page lists name, date of birth, AHV number, address, contact details, salary and pension data, civil status, partner details and IBAN as data that could be affected, while the AWP agency relays the supplier's position that the volume is rather small and the data may be business data. On 2026-10-09 the Bernische Pensionskasse, which insures canton of Bern staff and cantonal university personnel, said its supplier is the same company, and the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse and Pensionskasse Post reported the supplier incident too; none of the funds has yet confirmed which member data left, and the access vector and the actor are not public.
actions: Tell the helpdesk, HR and payroll teams of every body whose staff are insured with Publica (including the federal administration and the ETH domain) that AHV number, date of birth, address, salary and IBAN may now be known to criminals and must not count as proof of identity, and route requests that quote them, a request to change a payout account included, to a call-back on a known number; for staff insured with the Bernische Pensionskasse or the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse apply the same rule until those funds report the scope, because the Bernische Pensionskasse says it has no indication of theft but cannot exclude it and the Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse is still checking whether and to what extent its data is affected.

If your organisation's pension administration, HR or payroll runs on PK Softech software, is being migrated to it or tested on it, or your staff are insured with Pensionskasse Post, ask the supplier or the fund in writing whether your data, test data included, was in the affected environment and what it holds.

records.title: A fake WatchGuard VPN download site captures the SSL VPN server, login and password in the browser and then serves the genuine signed installer, leaving no malicious file for endpoint tools to flag
records.headline: Huntress: a lookalike VPN-client site harvests credentials, then hands over the real signed installer
records.summary: Huntress describes a lookalike WatchGuard VPN download site, reached on 2026-10-07 by an administrator at a managed service provider through a Bing search result, that asks for the SSL VPN server, login and password, rejects the first submission so the victim types again, and only then downloads the genuine, validly signed WatchGuard installer from WatchGuard's own CDN. No malware is delivered, so endpoint controls have no file to flag, and few reputation engines flagged the domains.

records.title: CVE-2026-110447, Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server (Nextcloud richdocumentscode app): an unauthenticated command injection in proxy.php, exploited in the wild to plant PHP web shells, fixed in 26.4.303 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)
records.headline: Exploited Nextcloud Collabora CODE app flaw: disabling the app does not help; update to 26.4.303 or remove it
records.summary: CVE-2026-110447 is an OS command injection in proxy.php of the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server, the richdocumentscode app that runs Collabora inside Nextcloud; versions before 26.4.303 are affected, the GitHub advisory record says it was exploited in the wild in September and October 2026, and a hoster reported web shells on its Nextcloud servers on 2026-09-11. Disabling the app does not stop the request, so it must be updated to 26.4.303 or removed; standalone Collabora Online servers are not affected.
actions: Update the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app (richdocumentscode) to 26.4.303 or remove it on every Nextcloud server that runs it; disabling the app does not stop the request, and on Nextcloud 29 or older, which is end of life, upgrade Nextcloud or remove the app.

On each such server, search the web access logs back to at least early September 2026 for requests to apps/richdocumentscode/proxy.php that carry $( or an encoded .. in the path, and the app directory for PHP files that are not part of the release; on a hit, treat every secret the web server account can read as exposed and rotate it.

records.title: CVE-2026-0322, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS: code injection in the management interface gives an authenticated attacker root, exploited in very limited attacks and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS-B 8.6)
records.headline: Palo Alto confirms limited exploitation of a PAN-OS management-interface root flaw; no workaround, 11.2.16 due 15 Oct
records.summary: Palo Alto Networks' advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-0322, a code injection in the PAN-OS management interface that lets an authenticated attacker with network access run code as root on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama; the advisory is tagged as attacked and reports very limited exploitation, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. There is no workaround, the risk is highest where the management interface is reachable from the internet, and the 11.2.16 build is listed with an ETA of 2026-10-15, so units on 11.2.14 and 11.2.15 had no fixed build at publication.
actions: Restrict the management interface of every PA-Series, VM-Series and Panorama to a jump box or trusted internal addresses now, then upgrade each to the fixed build of its train (11.2.14 and 11.2.15 units to 11.2.16, listed with an ETA of 2026-10-15); there is no workaround.

On every device whose management interface was reachable from untrusted networks, search management-interface logins, administrator-change records and upstream firewall logs for the three source addresses Palo Alto lists in the advisory's FAQ, and treat a match as a root compromise.

records.title: CVE-2026-76519, Cisco Secure Email Gateway: one crafted email attachment writes files and runs commands as root, exploited in the wild and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Cisco's mail gateway has a second exploited root flaw in four weeks; the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update
records.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-14 fixes CVE-2026-76519, a relative path traversal in the Advanced Malware Protection (file reputation) path of Cisco Secure Email Gateway that lets an unauthenticated attacker who sends one crafted attachment through the device write files and run commands as root (CVSS 9.8); Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of exploitation in October 2026, and CISA listed the flaw in KEV the same day. Only gateways with File Reputation enabled on a mail policy and Content Scanner Tools earlier than 25.3.0.5525 are exposed; there is no workaround, and the fix ships as a Content Scanner Tools update that needs no restart or upgrade, and in AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 and 16.5.0-780.
actions: Run contentscannerstatus on every Cisco Secure Email Gateway that has File Reputation enabled in a mail policy and update Content Scanner Tools to 25.3.0.5525 or later with contentscannerupdate wherever automatic updates are off; the update needs no restart.

On every such gateway, and on each member of a cluster, run grep "System Security" system_logs now: on a suspected-compromise message keep the forensic data before upgrading, then follow Cisco's recovery steps (a new virtual machine on a fixed release with a fresh configuration and renewed credentials for a virtual appliance, Cisco TAC for a physical one) for every member of that cluster.

records.title: Claroty Team82: 23 vulnerabilities in Copeland XWEB Pro supervisory refrigeration controllers chain to unauthenticated root RCE — a deterministic admin password derived from the device's own MAC address is one of THREE independent pre-auth paths
records.headline: An attacker can reconstruct admin credentials for an exposed refrigeration controller offline, then silently disable cooling while the display reports normal
records.summary: Claroty Team82 disclosed 23 vulnerabilities (21 high) in Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO supervisory refrigeration controllers. Three chain to unauthenticated root RCE: an auth-bypass logic flaw in the Lua authentication handler, a deterministic admin-password generator derivable offline from the device's MAC address and current date, and an unauthenticated OS command injection via the libraries installation route. 17 further, authenticated-only command-injection flaws are individually CVE-mapped by the source at CVSS 8.0 each. Copeland fixed all 23 in firmware v1.13; no source read reports exploitation of these flaws, but CERT-FR's alert of 2026-10-13 now reports numerous compromises of Copeland xweb refrigeration controllers without naming models, flaws or the entry vector.
actions: Upgrade every Copeland XWEB300D/500D/500B PRO controller to firmware v1.13 now, and treat any internet-exposed unit as a compromise-assessment candidate regardless of prior authentication controls: the deterministic-password path is fully reconstructable offline from data available at unauthenticated public endpoints, so a strong admin password alone did not protect an unpatched device.

last_update.summary: Rapid7 reported on 2026-10-13 that it reproduced arbitrary code execution on GitLab CE 19.4.1, published a proof of concept, and found no confirmed exploitation in the wild. The demonstrated path needs push access to a public project and then an unauthenticated CI lint request, so instances with open sign-up or public projects that untrusted users can write to are the exposed case.

records.title: CVE-2026-97229, GitLab CE/EE: an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler allows code execution on self-managed servers and now has a public proof of concept; fixed in 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8, and 19.4.1 does not close it (CVSS 10.0)
records.headline: GitLab's CVSS 10.0 CI regex flaw now has a public PoC; the demonstrated path needs push access to a public project
records.summary: GitLab's critical patch release of 2026-10-12 fixes CVE-2026-97229 (CVSS 3.1 10.0), an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler that lets code run on the server as the git user through a crafted expression in a CI/CD configuration; Rapid7 reported on 2026-10-13 that it reproduced it on 19.4.1 and published a proof of concept, and reports no confirmed exploitation in the wild. The demonstrated path needs push access to a public project (an ordinary account where users may create public projects), followed by a request to the CI lint API that carries no credentials. Self-managed CE and EE from 19.2 before 19.2.8, 19.3 before 19.3.5 and 19.4 before 19.4.2 are affected, and NCSC Switzerland and CERT-EU both published advisories on 2026-10-12.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed GitLab CE and EE instance on 19.2, 19.3 or 19.4 to 19.2.8, 19.3.5 or 19.4.2 now, internet-reachable instances and instances that allow open sign-up or public projects first, because a public proof of concept exists; 19.4.1 and 19.3.4 remain affected, and until each instance is upgraded, restrict anonymous access to public projects and stop untrusted users from creating or writing to public projects, which reduces exposure only to the path Rapid7 demonstrated.

records.title: Tangerhütte (Saxony-Anhalt): the vendor of the municipal citizen-portal software says attackers exploited a zero-day in it, classifies the intrusion as AI-driven, and four other communes took their portals offline
records.headline: German portal vendor reports an exploited zero-day and calls it AI-driven; police neither confirm nor deny that
records.summary: Innocon, the Tangermünde developer of the "digitales Rathaus" citizen portal, said in an MDR report of 2026-10-13 that attackers found and exploited a vulnerability it did not know of in its software, run for Tangerhütte on systems of the state municipal IT provider KID; the portal was taken offline in September and four more communes pulled theirs as a precaution. Innocon says the attackers reached only test accounts and took no real data, and classifies the intrusion as AI-driven because of command speed and on-host tool development, which is the vendor's reading: the state criminal police can neither confirm nor deny it. No CVE, product version or fix is named.

records.title: Adobe October 2026 bulletins: unauthenticated CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 flaws, most leading to code execution, in ColdFusion (APSB26-144), Experience Manager (APSB26-152) and Commerce and Magento (APSB26-153), none reported exploited
records.headline: Adobe fixes unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 flaws in ColdFusion, Experience Manager and Commerce; no exploitation known
records.summary: Adobe's 2026-10-13 bulletins fix five unauthenticated network flaws at CVSS 9.0 to 10.0 in ColdFusion 2025 and 2023 (fixed in 2025.0.14 and 2023.0.26), three unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 code-execution flaws in Experience Manager (Cloud Service 2026.9.28386 or per-issue hotfixes) and two code-execution flaws (CVSS 10.0 and 9.8) in Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source (2026-oct builds). Adobe says it knows of no exploitation of any of them; each needs no account, so exposure rather than exploitation status decides the order.
actions: Update every internet-facing ColdFusion server to 2025.0.14 or 2023.0.26, every AEM instance to Cloud Service 2026.9.28386 or the per-issue hotfixes for 6.5 Service Pack 25 and 6.5 LTS Service Pack 3, and Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source to the 2026-oct build of the installed 2.4.x line (together with the CVE-2026-75650 hotfix from the September APSB26-146 update where it is missing); Magento Open Source 2.4.6 has no listed fix.

records.title: CVE-2026-70571, Microsoft Exchange Server: an unauthenticated crafted-email code-execution flaw in the October 2026 security updates, the last Exchange 2016 and 2019 updates under the paid ESU (CVSS 8.1)
records.headline: Exchange October updates fix an unauthenticated email-borne RCE; 2016 and 2019 get their last update, and only with ESU
records.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 Exchange security updates fix CVE-2026-70571, a stack-based buffer overflow that an unauthenticated attacker can trigger with a crafted email (Critical, CVSS 8.1 with high attack complexity, Exploitation More Likely, not exploited), and CVE-2026-70279, a 9.3 cross-site scripting flaw that lets an attacker act as an administrator who clicks a crafted link. October is the last month Exchange 2016 and 2019 customers enrolled in the Period 2 ESU receive newly released updates, and organisations without ESU have no 2016 or 2019 update at all.
actions: Install the October 2026 Exchange security update on every Exchange server and on every machine that has the Exchange Management Tools; on Exchange 2016 and 2019 servers that are not covered by the Period 2 ESU, decide now between enrolling (it only gets an organisation current through this release) and moving to Exchange Subscription Edition, because after October Microsoft ships updates for Subscription Edition only.

records.title: CVE-2026-96951, Windows Shell: a Mark of the Web bypass exploited as a zero-day, fixed in the 2026-10-13 cumulative updates and listed in CISA KEV (CVSS 8.8)
records.headline: Microsoft patches an exploited Windows Shell zero-day that evades Mark of the Web protections on files and links
records.summary: Microsoft's 2026-10-13 updates fix CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell flaw that lets an attacker evade Mark of the Web defenses once a user opens a crafted file or link sent by email or instant message, so Windows does not show the dialog the tag normally triggers. Microsoft marks it exploited and CISA added it to KEV the same day; no source names the actor, the payload or the victims. Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 gets no patch, while Microsoft lists fixes for Server 2012 R2 and every later supported release.
actions: Deploy the 2026-10-13 cumulative update for each release (KB5127648 for Windows 11 24H2, 25H2 and 26H2, KB5127646 for Windows 11 26H1, KB5126657 for Windows 10 21H2 and 22H2, KB5126655 for Server 2022, KB5126646 for Server 2025, and the others listed in the CVE record) to every Windows endpoint and server, starting with the systems whose users open mail and chat attachments or download files; Rapid7 says Windows Server 2012 receives no patch.

records.title: CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, and the root-escalation step of the chain is still unpatched (CVSS 8.6)
records.headline: Ivanti Connect Secure zero-day chain is exploited; its root step has no fix and it evades the Integrity Checker
records.summary: Ivanti disclosed CVE-2026-104935 on 2026-10-13, an authentication bypass in Connect Secure that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker run commands, and says it is aware of limited exploitation; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Volexity found a cluster it calls UTA0576 chaining it with a root escalation that Ivanti has not yet fixed, patching library code in memory only so Ivanti's Integrity Checker Tool sees no file change, and going after the appliance's Active Directory service account, LAPS passwords and BitLocker recovery keys. Fixed builds are 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0 and 25.1.3.1, and 22.8R2.5; a patched appliance that was exposed still needs a compromise check.
actions: Upgrade every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance on 25.1.1.1 or earlier, 25.1.2.2 or earlier, or 22.8R2.4 or earlier to 25.1.1.2, 25.1.3.0 or 25.1.3.1, or 22.8R2.5 now, internet-facing appliances first; 22.7.x and below are not affected.

Run a compromise check on every appliance that was reachable on an affected build, starting with proxy, load balancer or WAF logs back to at least 2026-10-03 for welcome.cgi requests that carry an X-DSCGI-PATH header; where compromise cannot be excluded, follow Ivanti's recovery steps and then reset the domain service account, LAPS and local passwords, certificates and API keys the appliance held.

Previdian has not established that an attempt would have compromised a system, and SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation.

records.title: CVE-2026-102255, SonicWall SMA1000: a third unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 Work Place SSRF this year, affecting the hotfix builds that closed the September zero-days, with exploitation attempts reported that SonicWall has not confirmed
records.headline: NCSC.ch now rates the SonicWall SMA1000 pre-auth SSRF actively exploited; SonicWall still reports no evidence
records.summary: SonicWall's advisory SNWLID-2026-0017 (2026-10-06) fixes four SMA1000 flaws, led by CVE-2026-102255, a pre-authentication server-side request forgery in the Work Place interface (CVSS 3.0 10.0) that affects 12.4.3-03526 and 12.5.0-02952, the hotfixes issued for the September zero-days; fixed builds are 12.4.3-03670 and 12.5.0-03082. Two honeypot operators report exploitation attempts against the flaw, Defused from 2026-10-08 and Previdian from 2026-10-09, and NCSC Switzerland recorded it as actively exploited on 2026-10-12, without anyone establishing that an attempt would have compromised a system; SonicWall's advisory still says it has no evidence of exploitation. The two earlier unauthenticated Work Place SSRF flaws this year were exploited, each paired with an administrator-only command-execution flaw.
actions: Install SonicWall's platform hotfix 12.4.3-03670 or 12.5.0-03082 (or higher) on every SMA1000 6210, 7210 and 8200v, internet-reachable appliances first and including appliances already on the 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 hotfix from September; the appliance restarts when the installation finishes and no workaround is listed.

On every SMA1000 whose Work Place interface was internet-reachable before the hotfix, check its web access log back to 2026-10-06, the day the advisory was published, for the requests Previdian describes and, on a hit, run the compromise check SonicWall's earlier guidance describes.

MikroTik's own changelogs show both had already shipped: 7.23.8 on 2026-10-08 and 6.49.23 on 2026-10-07 each list the CVE-2026-84411 fix, so owners of long-term and v6 devices can upgrade instead of only restricting the web service.

records.title: CVE-2026-84411, MikroTik RouterOS: one unauthenticated request to the web management service can run code as root; fixed in 7.24 (v7 stable), 7.23.8 (v7 long-term) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term) (CVSS 3.1 9.8)
records.headline: MikroTik's long-term changelogs already carry the fix for a pre-auth RouterOS RCE; its notice still says pending
records.summary: MikroTik's notice of 2026-10-06 describes CVE-2026-84411, an integer underflow in HTTP request body handling of the RouterOS web management service (WebFig, on the www and www-ssl ports) that one crafted request sent without logging in can use to crash the service or run code on the router with full privileges; CISA scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8. RouterOS before 7.24, v6 included, is affected where an attacker can reach the web interface; 7.24 fixes the v7 stable channel and MikroTik's changelogs list the fix in 7.23.8 (v7 long-term, 2026-10-08) and 6.49.23 (v6 long-term, 2026-10-07), although its notice still shows both long-term releases as pending; MikroTik says the default firewall already blocks the web interface from the internet, and CISA records no known public exploitation.
actions: Find every RouterOS device whose www or www-ssl service answers from a network you do not trust and upgrade it to the fixed build for its channel: 7.24 or later on v7 stable, 7.23.8 on v7 long-term, 6.49.23 on v6 long-term; where an upgrade has to wait, restrict www and www-ssl under IP > Services to trusted addresses or disable them and manage the router over WinBox, SSH or a VPN.

records.title: CVE-2026-85097, Bricksforge for WordPress: an unauthenticated upload in the Pro Forms module writes attacker PHP into the uploads directory, exploited since 7 October; fixed in 4.0.1 and 3.1.8.10 (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Bricksforge's Pro Forms upload flaw is exploited without login since 7 October; fixed in 4.0.1 and 3.1.8.10
records.summary: Patchstack reports that CVE-2026-85097, an unauthenticated arbitrary file upload in the Pro Forms module of Bricksforge, a paid WordPress add-on for the Bricks page builder, has been targeted in the wild since 2026-10-07: it lets an attacker with no account get a PHP file written to the uploads directory and executed, on versions up to and including 3.1.8.9 with Pro Forms active (about 6,000 active installations). Bricksforge's changelog of 2026-10-08 lists the fix in 4.0.1 and Patchstack names 3.1.8.10 for the 3.x line; the exploitation report rests on Patchstack's telemetry.
actions: Find every WordPress site that your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run with Bricksforge and update it to version 4.0.1 (3.1.8.10 on the 3.x line) now, treating any site that was reachable and unpatched since 2026-10-07 as one to search for dropped PHP files.

records.title: Denmark's CPR population register: unauthorised parties abused a small private company's lawful lookup access, where Politiken reports at least three accounts used the password 123456, and obtained names, addresses and CPR numbers of 8.8 million people
records.headline: A Danish company's register access, reportedly secured with the password 123456, was abused to obtain 8.8 million CPR numbers
records.summary: Denmark's CPR administration says unauthorised parties used a private Danish company's lawful right to search the Central Person Register to obtain names, addresses and CPR numbers of about 8.8 million of its roughly 11 million records (living, deceased and emigrated persons); the ministry says the access does not cover the names and addresses of people with name-and-address protection. The company, Pays ApS of Odense, confirmed to TV 2 that its lawful access was abused, and Politiken reports that at least three of its accounts, including the administrator account, used the password 123456; Ritzau puts the access at 21 days and 17 hours from 10 September, where the minister had described about ten days. records.title: CHAINDROP — the Shai-Hulud npm worm returns through the keyv maintainer, backdoors 400+ packages, and resolves its exfiltration endpoint from an Ethereum smart contract
records.headline: A self-propagating npm worm reaches packages totalling 1.3 billion monthly downloads, and its C2 address lives on-chain
records.summary: Elastic Security Labs identified CHAINDROP on 2026-08-04, a new wave of the Shai-Hulud npm worm that began with the compromise of the keyv maintainer and has backdoored over 400 npm packages whose combined reach Elastic puts at more than 1.3 billion monthly downloads, keyv alone at over 600 million. Execution comes from a package.json preinstall hook that downloads the Bun runtime to run an obfuscated 711 KB payload, which harvests over 300 credential patterns — AI-assistant tokens, AWS/GCP/Azure/Alibaba credentials, GitHub tokens, Vault tokens, SSH keys and Kubernetes service-account tokens — and self-propagates only when it finds an npm token that both carries package-write permission and can publish without two-factor authentication. Rather than hardcoding a command-and-control domain, CHAINDROP queries an Ethereum smart contract at runtime to resolve where to send the stolen material, so the operator rotates infrastructure without shipping a new payload. On 2026-10-08 a release of the tensorlake npm SDK carried the same payload family with valid build provenance, and Socket and OX Security describe a dead-man switch that wipes the owner's home directory if the stolen GitHub token is revoked before its persistence is removed.
actions: Audit every npm publish token your organisation and its maintainers hold and revoke any that can publish without two-factor authentication — that exact token property, not package popularity, is what decides whether the worm spreads from a compromised developer to your packages.

On any developer workstation or build agent that installed a package from the keyv family since 2026-08-04, or tensorlake@0.5.144 since 2026-10-08, treat the AI-assistant, cloud, GitHub, Vault, SSH and Kubernetes credentials present on that host as disclosed and rotate them; the collector sweeps over 300 credential patterns in one pass, so partial rotation leaves the operator a working set. Isolate the host before revoking its GitHub token, because OX Security reports a switch that wipes the machine when the token is revoked; on a host that ran tensorlake@0.5.144, Socket and OX Security also name the gh-token-monitor persistence (a systemd user unit on Linux, a LaunchAgent on macOS, a scheduled task on Windows), which has to be removed before the token is revoked.

Stop treating a valid npm provenance attestation as evidence a package is clean; where release pipelines gate on provenance, change the check to pin on the workflow identity inside the Fulcio certificate and the Rekor log index, which is what Unit 42 says still discriminates.

records.title: IDC Frontier: ransomware stops four zones of IDCF Cloud for 495 companies and local governments, and the provider says customer data there can be restored only from customers' own backups
records.headline: IDCF Cloud ransomware hits 495 customers incl. local governments; provider says only their own backups restore
records.summary: IDC Frontier, a SoftBank Group subsidiary, says a ransomware attack from about 3:40 a.m. on 2026-10-07 stopped four zones of its IDCF Cloud East Japan Region 1, affecting 495 companies and local governments whose virtual servers stopped and cannot be restarted. Its third report (2026-10-08) says customer data in those zones is expected to be difficult to retrieve or restore and, in its current view, can be recovered only from customers' own backups; management consoles are suspended in every region and the intrusion route is not public. Municipal and prefectural websites were among those that went down.

records.title: PoeLLM: a cryptomining botnet that reads its C2 address out of a GitHub poem compromises exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers and turns them into scanners
records.headline: Lumen: a botnet takes its C2 address from a GitHub poem and spreads through exposed AI and developer servers
records.summary: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs tracks PoeLLM, a financially motivated botnet active since at least April 2026 that Lumen says has impacted more than 3,400 servers, mostly in the United States and Western Europe, among them exposed LiteLLM, Ollama, Gotenberg and Gitea servers, with Ivanti Sentry possibly targeted. The malware derives its command-and-control address from words in a poem in a GitHub repository, runs XMRig and Iron miners and turns victims into scanners and exploit launchers that Lumen says likely abuse the LiteLLM CVE-2026-42271 path.

records.title: Attackers compromised the .gh, .sl and .as country-code registries, rewrote authoritative DNS and obtained valid HTTPS certificates for Google and YouTube names
records.headline: Registry-level DNS hijacks of .gh, .sl and .as produced valid HTTPS certificates for Google names
records.summary: Google's Chrome team reported on 2026-10-06 that attackers compromised the .gh, .sl and .as country-code registries, changed authoritative DNS records and obtained unauthorized HTTPS certificates for Google domains and for domains of other organizations; Chrome blocked them and Google had the issuing authorities revoke the Google certificates. Google names no attacker or entry vector and says it cannot guarantee it found every affected domain; The Hacker News found 12 certificates for Google and YouTube names in public logs, 11 issued by Let's Encrypt and one by ZeroSSL, first logged between 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-27.

records.title: GhostAction returns: stolen maintainer credentials push a fake security-audit workflow into the victims' own GitHub repositories, which now harvests credentials from the entire git history
records.headline: GhostAction: fake security workflows now harvest whole git histories; rotating Actions secrets is not enough
records.summary: StepSecurity and Socket report that on 2026-10-08 the GhostAction campaign used the GitHub credentials of two open-source maintainers to commit a workflow disguised as a security audit straight to the default branch of 345 to 346 repositories, including one of an Uber-owned organisation, and that the workflow now sends the credentials found in the working tree and in the entire git history, besides the named Actions secrets, to a hardcoded address over plain HTTP. StepSecurity read a run log showing the exfiltration was acknowledged four seconds after the run started; no malicious package release from the stolen credentials has been seen yet.
actions: Run an organisation-scoped GitHub code search in every organisation your teams and suppliers administer for workflow files under .github/workflows that present themselves as a security audit, a security check or an Actions security workflow and were added since 2026-08-31; any hit means assume breach: revoke the credential that committed it and rotate every secret found anywhere in the repository's git history, not only the configured Actions secrets.

records.title: CVE-2026-105133 / CVE-2026-105134, AhsayCBS backup management console: an unauthenticated authentication-bypass and code-execution chain exploited since 7 October to drop webshells and a cryptominer, with 10.3.4 also affected and no fixed release named
records.headline: Huntress: AhsayCBS flaws are exploited for SYSTEM-level code execution, and 10.3.4 is also affected
records.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-10-07 23:20 UTC attackers chaining two AhsayCBS flaws, CVE-2026-105133 (authentication bypass) and CVE-2026-105134 (code execution as SYSTEM through the Replication Receiver API), against internet-exposed servers of the backup management console that managed service providers and system integrators mainly use, dropping JSP webshells and an XMRig cryptominer; BleepingComputer reports at least five organizations targeted and a public exploit for the first flaw. Public records listed versions up to 10.3.2 as affected, but Huntress found on 2026-10-08 that 10.3.4, which BleepingComputer calls the latest version, is also affected, and no fixed release is named, so restricting the management interface is the interim control.
actions: Find every AhsayCBS server your organisation or your managed-service suppliers run and put its management web interface behind a VPN or an allowlist of trusted addresses now: Huntress found 10.3.4, which BleepingComputer calls the latest version, also affected, so upgrading is not a mitigation until Ahsay names a fixed release.

On any AhsayCBS server that was internet-reachable since 2026-10-04, check for the artifacts Huntress describes (children of the service downloading into Temp folders, new .jsp files in the application directory, a service that mimics the Edge updater) and re-image a host with a confirmed compromise from a trusted backup, as Huntress advises.

records.title: SAP September 2026 Patch Day: OVERPASS (CVE-2026-44756, CVSS 10.0) and S4GET (CVE-2026-58240, CVSS 9.8) — two unauthenticated pre-auth RCE flaws in shared SAP kernel components reachable through ports that cannot be firewalled without breaking normal SAP GUI/RFC use
records.headline: Two maximum-severity SAP kernel flaws are reachable through the same ports every SAP GUI and RFC client needs — network segmentation alone will not close them
records.summary: SAP's 8 September 2026 Patch Day fixed CVE-2026-44756 (OVERPASS, CVSS 10.0), an unauthenticated memory-corruption flaw in kernel Extended Passport processing reachable via the web tier, SAP Dispatcher or RFC, and CVE-2026-58240 (S4GET, CVSS 9.8), an unauthenticated Message Server trust-bypass reachable on the port every SAP GUI client uses; both yield unauthenticated remote code execution across the SAP kernel-based product line. Neither is yet confirmed exploited, but Onapsis found over 10,000 internet-facing SAP interfaces, and since 2026-09-15 an open-source SAP exploitation toolkit, SAPMAP, has carried proof-of-concept exploits for both flaws.
actions: Apply SAP Security Notes 3747649 (OVERPASS) and 3759472 (S4GET) to every SAP kernel-based system now, internet-exposed systems first and then internal ones, because the affected components are commonly reachable through internal firewalls; public proof-of-concept exploits for both flaws have been available since 2026-09-15 in the SAPMAP toolkit, and Onapsis found over 10,000 internet-facing SAP interfaces.

records.title: CVE-2026-82078 / CVE-2026-81578 — PaperCut NG/MF: an Apache Tapestry request-routing confusion chains an unauthenticated config rewrite to arbitrary code execution, exploited before a patch existed
records.headline: A pre-auth RCE chain in PaperCut NG/MF was exploited before any patch existed; tested maintenance releases now replace three emergency patches
records.summary: PaperCut NG and PaperCut MF (all versions) carry an unauthenticated remote-code-execution chain — CVE-2026-81578 (auth bypass, CVSS4.0 8.8) and CVE-2026-82078 (unsafe dynamic class loading, CVSS4.0 9.4) — that PaperCut confirmed under active exploitation on 2026-08-27, before any CVE or patch existed. Fully tested maintenance releases 26.0.5, 25.0.13 and 24.1.10 (10 September 2026) replace the emergency patches and are the vendor's recommended build; servers still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2 need to upgrade now. There is no fix for v23 and earlier, and Huntress estimates 47% of the PaperCut installs it tracks run v23 or older. GreyNoise now documents an AI-agent-orchestrated mass-exploitation campaign against this same chain, compromising at least 440 instances across 395 identified organizations since 31 August 2026, reaching full domain admin in as little as five minutes via legacy Active Directory escalation paths. watchTowr's write-up of 2026-10-09 shows the 28 August emergency build could still be taken without authentication through the Setup Wizard forms, and names CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor lists as fixed only in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13.
actions: Upgrade every PaperCut NG/MF Application Server, Site Server and secondary/print server to the security maintenance release for its line (26.0.5, 25.0.13 or 24.1.10), starting with any still on Emergency Patch Release 1 or 2, and note that the emergency builds do not carry the fix for CVE-2026-82077, an administrator-only Scan-to-Fax code-execution flaw that the vendor's September bulletin lists as fixed in 26.0.5 and 25.0.13 and does not list for 24.1.10; for v23 and earlier, immediately restrict the Application Server's web interface to trusted/internal IP addresses only; no patch exists for that line.

Before patching or restarting an internet-facing server, preserve the server/logs directory and process tree; check server.log for the two vendor-documented error strings and for an unexplained gap or truncation, check derby.log for a Derby boot line naming an in-memory database directory ending in "pwn", and hunt for a Windows service named "Remote Access Service" running SimpleService.exe (SimpleHelp) or an unexpected AnyDesk install, as PaperCut's own published incident data names both as an observed post-compromise access method.

Given GreyNoise's confirmed domain-admin escalation paths, verify no PaperCut Application Server is domain-joined with a privileged service account or hosted on a domain controller, and confirm domain controllers reachable from any PaperCut host are patched against the 2021 noPac flaws (CVE-2021-42278/CVE-2021-42287); GreyNoise reports the AI-orchestrated campaign reaching full domain admin through these paths in as little as five minutes after initial access.

records.title: CVE-2026-102489 / CVE-2026-102490, Zammad helpdesk: a session-hijack remote code execution and a zammad-to-root escalation, both reported exploited since 21 September; 7.2.2 fixes the root flaw on DEB and RPM installs
records.headline: Zammad 7.2.2 fixes the exploited zammad-to-root escalation on DEB and RPM installs; the session-leak RCE has a public exploit
records.summary: DIVD, the Dutch vulnerability-disclosure CSIRT, says attackers entered its network on 2026-09-21 through two Zammad flaws it calls previously unknown: CVE-2026-102489, a session hijack leading to code execution as the zammad user in versions 6.3.0 to 6.5.4, and CVE-2026-102490, a local escalation from that user to root. NCSC-NL states both have been exploited since 21 September and CISA listed both in KEV on 2026-10-02; Zammad says the code-execution flaw is exploitable only on 6.5 and older, which receive no security fixes, and Horizon3 published the root cause and a working exploit for it on 2026-10-07. Zammad 7.2.2 (2026-10-08) fixes the root escalation, which affects only DEB and RPM (packager.io) installations; it follows 7.2.1 (2026-10-06), which fixed 27 newly published advisories in 7.2.0 and earlier, two rated critical, none with a CVE id and none reported exploited.
actions: Copy the application and network logs of every self-hosted Zammad instance, then upgrade it to Zammad 7.2.2 (6.5 and older receive no security fixes, and 7.2.0 is affected by the 27 advisories Zammad published on 2026-10-06) or take it offline if it cannot be upgraded.

On every instance that was internet-reachable on 6.3.0 to 6.5.4 since 2026-09-21, run DIVD's log-check script, and treat a hit, or any DEB or RPM host where code ran as the zammad account, as compromised.

records.title: TraderTraitor (Jade Sleet) backdoors resurface on a non-cryptocurrency IT-services firm in a campaign that delivers malware through weaponized Terraform provider lockfiles, resolving C2 through a Nostr-relay dead drop
records.headline: SentinelLabs: the same DPRK backdoors from a $292M crypto theft resurface on a victim with no crypto ties, in a campaign that uses poisoned Terraform lockfiles
records.summary: SentinelLabs found the FLATROOF and ROOFDECK macOS backdoors, first documented in April 2026's USD 292 million LayerZero/KelpDAO cryptocurrency theft, on an unrelated victim: a small India-based IT-services provider with no cryptocurrency ties. The campaign's fake job-interview GitHub repositories carry weaponized Terraform provider lockfiles that redirect `terraform init` to attacker-controlled provider registries, though SentinelLabs cannot prove how this victim's backdoors were delivered. Zscaler ThreatLabz independently reports a July 2026 trojanized Terraform provider binary that runs malicious code as soon as Terraform loads it and delivers the same two families on macOS, Linux and Windows, which it suspects is TraderTraitor. The second-stage backdoor resolves its command-and-control address by reading an operator profile's public "website" field from the Nostr decentralized relay network.

records.title: CVE-2026-88771 / CVE-2026-88772, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: unauthenticated pre-auth RCE zero-days exploited before a patch existed (CVSS 4.0 9.5)
records.headline: Citrix confirms in-the-wild exploitation of two default-configuration NetScaler zero-days and publishes no workaround
records.summary: Citrix's CTX697096 bulletin (2026-09-27) fixes eight NetScaler ADC/Gateway flaws, two of which, CVE-2026-88771 (unauthenticated command execution, every default deployment) and CVE-2026-88772 (memory overflow to RCE/DoS, reachable wherever DTLS is enabled, the VPN-vServer default), were already being exploited in the wild before any fix existed. CISA added both to KEV the same day; Citrix lists no workaround. Google's Mandiant and GTIG report a campaign running since at least early September that leaves web-server-configuration persistence on compromised appliances, so an appliance patched after the bulletin still needs a compromise check. Unit 42 telemetry adds version fingerprinting from 2026-08-21, web shells dropped as .deb packages from 2026-09-04 and a log-poisoning chain with concrete log artifacts to hunt. A separate Citrix bulletin of 2026-10-03 adds CVE-2026-88779, a SAML-triggered flaw these builds do not fix: SAML-configured appliances must move to 14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28, and a bulletin of 2026-10-08 adds CVE-2026-107406 for the same SAML configurations, so identity-provider appliances need 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29.
actions: Upgrade every internet-facing NetScaler ADC/Gateway to 14.1-73.37+ (14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.37 FIPS+) or 13.1-64.23+ (13.1-FIPS/NDcPP 13.1-37.279+) now (a SAML-configured appliance needs the later builds named for CVE-2026-88779, and an identity provider 14.1-73.46 or 13.1-64.29); on a 13.1-branch appliance run `show ns variable` first; if it returns any variables, install 13.1-64.24 instead to avoid a known reboot loop. Capture logs, an instance snapshot where the appliance is virtual, a support bundle and a core dump from each exposed appliance BEFORE patching, since the upgrade can remove forensic evidence of prior exploitation.

Run Mandiant's compromise checks, extended by the Unit 42 artifacts described in the update below, on every NetScaler that was internet-facing and unpatched at any time since early September, patched or not; isolate any hit and halt HA configuration sync until both nodes are validated.

Find any NetScaler ADC or Gateway still on the end-of-life 12.1 or 13.0 branches and decide isolation or replacement now: they receive no security updates and Citrix has not said whether they are affected.

records.title: CVE-2026-88779, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: a SAML-triggered memory overflow still hits appliances on the September fixed builds, and Citrix confirms targeted attacks (CVSS 4.0 8.7)
records.headline: Citrix confirms attacks on a new NetScaler SAML flaw that the September fixed builds do not close
records.summary: Citrix's bulletin CTX697174 fixes CVE-2026-88779, a memory overflow in NetScaler ADC and Gateway that a network attacker needing no privileges reaches when the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider; Citrix says it has observed targeted attacks and scopes the impact to denial of service. Appliances already on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds that fixed the September zero-days remain affected and must move to 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28 or the FIPS builds, and identity-provider appliances then need 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29 or the FIPS builds, which close the further SAML flaw CVE-2026-107406 that Citrix disclosed on 2026-10-08. Reports of code execution on patched honeypots are unconfirmed, and CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog on 2026-10-04.
actions: Upgrade every SAML-configured NetScaler (`add authentication samlAction` or `add authentication samlIdPProfile`) that is still below 14.1-73.41, 13.1-64.28, 14.1-73.41 FIPS or 13.1-37.282, including appliances on the 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 builds, to at least those builds; identity providers then need the builds named for CVE-2026-107406. Where the upgrade has to wait and NetScaler Console virtual patching is available, confirm with `show appfw signatures` that the Global Deny List signature version is at least v24, which Citrix offers as a bridge for CVE-2026-88779 only.

Before restarting a SAML-configured NetScaler that has crashed or rebooted repeatedly, preserve its logs and crash artifacts and open a Citrix support case, which Citrix asks for when an appliance is experiencing the impact.

records.title: ReliaQuest: LLM-driven agents run most of an intrusion through one unauthenticated Spring Batch job-submission feature on Apache Tomcat, from in-process JavaScript to SYSTEM in under 24 hours
records.headline: ReliaQuest: AI agents took a Tomcat server to SYSTEM in under a day through an exposed job-submission feature
records.summary: ReliaQuest assesses with high confidence that LLM-driven agents carried out substantial parts of an intrusion it investigated, using only known techniques: an internet-facing Apache Tomcat application accepted Spring Batch job definitions without a login, jobs ran JavaScript through the Nashorn engine inside the application process, plaintext SQL Server sysadmin credentials from the application's configuration led to xp_cmdshell, and two public privilege-escalation tools reached SYSTEM. ReliaQuest names no victim, sector or region, nor the vendor of the exposed application, and could not determine how many agents ran, which model drove them or how much a person approved.

records.title: Cisco Talos: malware now embeds natural-language instructions aimed at LLM triage pipelines, from a copied comment to template-sprayed prompts across four families, and a Russia-aligned group uses it too
records.headline: Talos: malware tells the analysing LLM to skip it; the text is plain and therefore detectable
records.summary: Cisco Talos documents 84 samples from four malware families, collected from January 2025 to July 2026, that embed plain natural-language text meant to steer the LLM stage of automated triage: a verbatim "no need to analyze this file" comment reused by at least four actors, templated variants, instructions repeated across seven chat-template formats, and intimidation or fabricated-authority text. ESET separately found UAC-0099 using a decoy request in a script comment to trip an LLM scanner's refusal; Talos' own test of five local models put the best techniques at steering the outcome in the attacker's favour in about 35% of runs, and its advice is to treat text inside a sample as evidence, never as instruction.

records.title: AA26-281A: China-linked actors enabled by Integrity Technology Group scan with MicroScan, spray Exchange and Microsoft 365 passwords and steal mail, and five old flaws from the scanner's scripts enter CISA KEV
records.headline: Joint advisory: Flax Typhoon-consistent actors spray Exchange and Microsoft 365, steal mail and keep SoftEther access
records.summary: The FBI, CISA, NSA, NCSC UK and partners from five more countries published AA26-281A on 2026-10-08 on China-linked actors enabled by Integrity Technology Group, whose tactics the advisory calls consistent with Flax Typhoon: open-source and MicroScan vulnerability scanning, XSS credential harvesting, password spraying against Exchange and Microsoft 365 interfaces, SoftEther VPN persistence, DCSync and bulk mail theft through Exchange Web Services. Five of the eight old flaws the advisory lists as successfully exploited (ProFTPD, ISC BIND, Apache Struts, ONLYOFFICE Docs, Strapi) were added to CISA's KEV catalog the same day; the FBI also seized the domains behind MicroScan and the FishHub phishing tool.

records.title: CVE-2026-107406, Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: a SAML-path memory overflow that can lead to code execution still affects the 2026-10-03 fixed builds on identity-provider appliances (CVSS 4.0 9.5)
records.headline: Citrix: a new NetScaler SAML overflow, rated Critical, reaches the builds that fixed the previous one
records.summary: Citrix's bulletin CTX697191 (2026-10-08, severity Critical) fixes CVE-2026-107406, a memory overflow in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway that leads to remote code execution or denial of service (CVSS 4.0 9.5) when the appliance is configured as a SAML service provider or identity provider. An identity-provider appliance is affected through the 14.1-73.41 and 13.1-64.28 builds that Citrix named for CVE-2026-88779 and must move to 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29 or the FIPS builds; Citrix says it is not aware of any unmitigated exploits.
actions: Upgrade each SAML identity-provider NetScaler (`add authentication samlIdPProfile`) straight to 14.1-73.46, 13.1-64.29, 14.1-73.46 FIPS or 13.1.37.283 (13.1-FIPS and NDcPP), including appliances already on 14.1-73.41 or 13.1-64.28; a service-provider-only appliance (`add authentication samlAction`) below 14.1-73.37 or 13.1-64.23 (FIPS and NDcPP: 13.1-37.279) needs the same builds.

records.title: CVE-2026-104286, Fortinet FortiMail: unauthenticated path traversal file write exploited as a zero-day, fixed in 8.0.2, 7.6.7 and 7.4.9 (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Fortinet now names fixed FortiMail builds for an unauthenticated file-write flaw it confirmed exploited as a zero-day
records.summary: Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-26-175 of 2026-10-01 describes a path traversal in FortiMail that lets an unauthenticated attacker write arbitrary files through crafted HTTP or HTTPS requests, and says it has been reported exploited in the wild; CISA listed it in KEV the same day. Belnet, the Belgian government and research network, says a zero-day in its supplier Fortinet's technology let attackers copy its inbound mail from 2026-07-22 and links this advisory, which puts exploitation about ten weeks before the disclosure. Fortinet's revision of 2026-10-05 names the fixed builds 8.0.2, 7.6.7 and 7.4.9 and tells 7.2 users to move to branch 7.4 or above; the vendor workarounds remain the interim control. Fortinet says it remediated FortiMail Cloud on 2026-10-05, so only self-managed appliances need action.
actions: Upgrade every self-managed FortiMail to the fixed build for its branch (8.0.2, 7.6.7 or 7.4.9; 7.2 moves to branch 7.4 or above, which means 7.4.9 or later; FortiMail Cloud customers need not act); until each appliance is upgraded, disable IBE support (config system encryption ibe, set status disable) or, as Fortinet's alternatives, cut the webmail interface off from the internet or block POST requests to /ibe containing '../' at a web application firewall in front of it.

Check every FortiMail that was internet-reachable before the workaround against the cron, CLI-audit and log artifacts in FG-IR-26-175 and the file artifacts that BleepingComputer and NCSC Switzerland describe, looking back to at least 2026-07-22, including a mail archive account that sends to a remote host and mail copied to destinations outside the organization.

records.title: FortiBleed: an active credential-compromise campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls, now locking administrators out and supplying ransomware affiliates
records.headline: FBI and Secret Service: FortiBleed is still active, locks admins out of FortiGates and feeds ransomware affiliates
records.summary: FortiBleed is an active credential-compromise campaign against internet-facing FortiGate firewalls and SSL VPN gateways, with SOCRadar counting more than 86,644 compromised devices in 194 countries; Fortinet said in June that it uses no new vulnerability, only reused credentials and brute force. A joint FBI and U.S. Secret Service advisory of 2026-10-06 says attackers keep scanning exposed devices with previously obtained credentials, create administrator accounts on compromised firewalls and in some cases delete or change the original accounts so owners are locked out, and that access brokers using the chain have supplied INC/Lynx and Payload ransomware affiliates. An organisation with an internet-exposed FortiGate should end all administrator and VPN sessions, reset every credential and look for accounts and API keys it did not create.
actions: On every internet-facing FortiGate, terminate all administrator and VPN sessions, reset every administrator and VPN password, review the local administrator list and the REST API keys for entries nobody created (the actors add administrator accounts for persistence and may delete or lock the original ones), restrict management access to trusted hosts or a local-in policy, and enforce PBKDF2 for administrator password storage as Fortinet's guidance describes for FortiOS 7.2.11 and later.

records.title: CVE-2026-21589, Atlassian Data Center: unauthenticated arbitrary file access in every version of eight self-managed products, patch or take them off the internet (CVSS 4.0 9.3)
records.headline: Atlassian file-read flaw: exploit attempts began the day of the public write-up; a scanning template exists
records.summary: Atlassian's advisory of 2026-10-05 fixes CVE-2026-21589, an unauthenticated arbitrary file access flaw in every version of Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center, plus Crucible and Fisheye (CVSS 4.0 9.3), and tells customers to patch immediately or take internet-facing instances off the internet. watchTowr Labs published the root cause, the request shape and a runnable checker on 2026-10-06, and exploitation attempts followed the same day: Previdian's sensors have recorded at least 129 attempts from at least 22 addresses, SANS ISC recorded similar attempts on its own honeypots, and a Nuclei template exists; neither honeypot operator reports a compromise. Where Jira is integrated with Crowd, the file read exposes a plaintext Crowd application password that gives access to Crowd as an administrator of that application.
actions: Upgrade every Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Service Management, Jira Software, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center installation to a fixed version of its line (Bitbucket 9.4.26, 10.2.8 or 10.5.1; Confluence 9.2.26 or 10.2.19; Jira Service Management 5.12.40, 10.3.26 or 11.3.12; Jira Software 9.12.40, 10.3.26 or 11.3.12; Bamboo 10.2.24 or 12.1.12; Crowd 6.3.7, 7.0.3, 7.1.7 or 7.2.4) and Crucible and Fisheye to 4.9.15, internet-reachable instances first; until each is upgraded, take it off the internet or put Atlassian's web application firewall or Tomcat rewrite rule in front of it.

On every Jira instance that was internet-reachable and unpatched and is integrated with Crowd, treat the Crowd application password in its WEB-INF/classes/crowd.properties as readable: rotate it after the upgrade and review Crowd for user accounts created or group memberships changed since the exposure began; on every affected instance search the web server and proxy logs back to 2026-10-05, the day the advisory published (honeypots recorded the first attempts on 2026-10-06), for '..' next to '/', '\\' or '::'.

records.title: BigDiskBuster: a roughly 300-line Windows proof of concept keeps Microsoft Defender from updating by claiming all free disk space, with no CVE and no patch
records.headline: A Defender bypass that needs no vulnerability: fill the disk during every update and the engine stays up, stale
records.summary: LevelBlue SpiderLabs reproduced BigDiskBuster, a proof of concept published on GitHub on 2026-09-19 by the actor known as MSNightmare, which watches the C: volume for Defender update activity and claims the free space so each update fails while the Defender service keeps running and real-time protection stays on. It runs from a standard account and has no CVE or patch; Microsoft says Defender Antivirus detects the proof of concept, and no use in attacks is reported.

records.title: A phishing link on Microsoft's own Power BI domain slips past mail filters and installs rogue ScreenConnect clients, then, in one incident, a script replaces the first remote-management tool with a second
records.headline: Huntress: a Power BI-hosted phishing link installs rogue ScreenConnect clients; in one case a script removed the first
records.summary: Huntress describes a phishing campaign seen since 2026-09-10 in which an Outlook email links to a fake reference document on a legitimate Power BI domain; a "Download Reference" button opens an attacker page that fingerprints the visitor and then downloads a ScreenConnect installer. The installer deploys a rogue ScreenConnect client that establishes a second one, and in one incident a PowerShell script removed the first; Huntress could not obtain the original email, and the configuration of one of the rogue clients also appeared on 22 other endpoints.

records.title: Ixa Systems, a Vaud security integrator serving police, prisons and banks: camera locations, plans and some passwords that TheGentlemen claimed to have stolen are reported on sale on the darknet
records.headline: Site plans, camera locations and some credentials of Vaud prisons and banks, and of police premises, reported for sale
records.summary: Le Temps reports, and the AWP news agency names the firm as Ixa Systems of Crissier (Vaud), that data stolen from a video-surveillance, alarm and access-control integrator is on sale on the darknet; the group TheGentlemen claimed the theft at the end of August. The loot reportedly includes camera locations, security-installation plans and, in some cases, usernames or passwords, for clients including police authorities, gendarmerie premises, prisons, hospitals, schools and banks; the reports do not state the access vector or list every affected site.
actions: If your organisation bought video-surveillance, alarm or access-control installation or maintenance from Ixa Systems, ask the firm in writing which of your sites and credentials are in the stolen data and rotate every camera, alarm, intercom and remote-maintenance credential it held.

records.title: The FBI says the incident at its recruitment portal resulted from a contractor failing to apply an issued security patch on a third-party-managed platform; sources name PeopleSoft, and ShinyHunters claimed the breach
records.headline: FBI: a contractor's missed security patch on a third-party platform caused the portal breach ShinyHunters claimed
records.summary: The extortion group ShinyHunters claims it exploited Oracle PeopleSoft to compromise the FBI's recruitment site (apply.fbijobs.gov), then pivoted into FBI-managed AWS GovCloud infrastructure and stole employee and applicant data; it told BleepingComputer it used the URL-encoded WAF bypass for the known PeopleSoft flaw CVE-2026-35273 and still claims a further unknown flaw. On 2026-10-06 the FBI's cyber chief said the incident resulted from a security failure of a platform managed by a third-party organization after a contractor failed to implement a security patch explicitly issued to secure it, and that the FBI has removed the contractor; Reuters' sources, as relayed by SecurityWeek, name Oracle PeopleSoft and Accenture, and the FBI names neither. Reuters reports psychiatric and medical files in the documents the group shared, Nextgov/FCW reports, citing two people familiar with the matter, that the data covers intelligence analysts and Remote Operations Unit personnel, and Nextgov/FCW relays Reuters' report of a suspected member detained in Jordan who is helping investigators.

records.title: CL-STA-1178 (Blinder Tunnel): an Iranian-nexus recruitment lure delivers a Visual Studio project that runs code when it is opened, then hijacks the .NET AppDomainManager, disables ETW and takes tasking from GitHub
records.headline: Unit 42: a coding-test Visual Studio project executes on open, then disables ETW and takes tasking from GitHub
records.summary: Unit 42 describes a March 2026 campaign by an Iranian-nexus cluster it calls CL-STA-1178 against an individual in Iraqi critical infrastructure, in which a recruiter persona impersonating Dubai Airports IT sent a coding-test Visual Studio project whose project file runs code during the design-time build, before any compile. The chain then hijacks the .NET AppDomainManager through a configuration file that disables ETW, sideloads a DLL, and uses the GitHub API and issue comments for command and control, with PowerShell run inside the hijacked process so no powershell.exe starts. No Swiss or European target is reported and Unit 42 is the only source.

records.title: A Gentlemen ransomware affiliate ran his own leak site and reached his victims through stolen CI/CD secrets, with attack commands driven through an MCP server (CloudSEK)
records.headline: CloudSEK: a Gentlemen affiliate reached victims through stolen GitLab CI/CD secrets and drove attacks over MCP
records.summary: CloudSEK analysed two exposed servers of "Azazel", a Russian-speaking affiliate of the Gentlemen ransomware group who also ran his own leak site, and reports about 6 TB of stolen data from some two dozen organisations, among them government-adjacent infrastructure. It says every confirmed victim was reached through stolen CI/CD secrets, mainly GitLab variable stores and git history, that one deeper intrusion into an AI platform chained server-side request forgery, a recovered master key that decrypted the configuration and a token recovered from git history, and that Azazel drove attack commands through an MCP server on a local port. The report is a single source and names no victim.

records.title: CVE-2026-94504 / CVE-2026-93836, Ninja Forms and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce: stored XSS exploited to plant a hidden WordPress administrator and four persistence routes that survive the update
records.headline: Exploited WordPress plugin XSS ends in a hidden admin and persistence that patching does not remove
records.summary: Patchstack reports that since 2026-10-04 one campaign has been exploiting two unrelated stored cross-site scripting flaws, CVE-2026-93836 in WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce up to 8.6.6 and CVE-2026-94504 in Ninja Forms up to 3.15.3, by planting a script in an order or a form submission that runs when a logged-in administrator opens it. The script uses the administrator's own session to install a malicious plugin and create administrators, one of them hidden from the Users screen, and leaves four independent ways back in, so updating to Ninja Forms 3.15.4 or WPC Product Bundles 8.6.7 stops new injections but does not evict an implant. Patchstack says exploitation volume is limited so far and that the second stage works with any stored XSS that reaches an administrator.
actions: Update Ninja Forms to 3.15.4 or later and WPC Product Bundles for WooCommerce to 8.6.7 or later on every WordPress site, then check each site for an implant the update does not remove, starting with a comparison of the database's administrator list against the Users screen and an inspection of the must-use plugins directory by content.

On any site where an administrator opened a Ninja Forms submission or a WooCommerce order since 2026-10-04 and an implant turns up, rotate all privileged credentials and the WordPress authentication salts and treat the oldest administrator account as compromised, because a login URL planted by the implant authenticates as that account.

records.title: CVE-2026-0257, Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect: pre-auth authentication bypass via certificate reuse, marked by CISA as used in ransomware campaigns
records.headline: CISA marks the exploited GlobalProtect VPN bypass as used in ransomware; Arctic Wolf traced Qilin intrusions to it
records.summary: CVE-2026-0257 is a pre-auth VPN authentication bypass in PAN-OS GlobalProtect (CISA KEV; Palo Alto reports limited exploit attempts, and Rapid7 and Unit 42 report successful exploitation): an attacker forges valid auth-override cookies by re-using the GlobalProtect certificate shared with the HTTPS service, with no credentials. CISA's KEV catalog (version 2026.10.04) marks it as used in known ransomware campaigns, and Arctic Wolf's report of 2026-07-20 describes June 2026 intrusions in which Qilin ransomware deployment began with this bypass. Patch or disable auth-override cookies, and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched as a compromise-assessment target.
actions: Patch every PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway to the fixed release in Palo Alto's advisory for its train, or disable authentication override cookies or give them a certificate that no other service uses, then force one re-authentication so override cookies regenerate.

On every GlobalProtect gateway that was internet-reachable and unpatched at any time since 2026-05-17, treat the network behind it as a ransomware compromise-assessment target: review VPN sessions that authenticated by cookie from unexpected sources, then check Windows hosts for the artifacts Arctic Wolf describes (a ransomware payload staged under C:\\PerfLogs, a PsExec service, an LSASS dump written through comsvcs.dll to an .odt file, an ntdsutil media copy of the Active Directory database, and cleared event logs).

records.title: CVE-2026-73570, Zimbra Collaboration: a pre-auth command injection patched without a CVE in July is exploited, with probing before disclosure and root escalation, secret theft and cluster-wide movement observed
records.headline: Fixed on 20 July, identified on 13 August, probed from 28 July: a CVE-keyed patch process never saw this one coming
records.summary: Zimbra shipped ZCS 10.1.20 on 2026-07-20 with a fix for a command injection in the SNMP monitoring component, and the identifier CVE-2026-73570 followed on 2026-08-13. Microsoft Threat Intelligence now reports confirmed intrusions in more than one region and industry, with probing of the injection point from 2026-07-28, before disclosure, and CISA lists the flaw in KEV (added 2026-08-21). The flaw needs no authentication and applies only where the optional zimbra-snmp package is installed and SNMP notifications are enabled; Microsoft's cases combined web shells, root escalation, theft of Zimbra's authentication keys and cluster-wide movement, so an upgrade does not evict an attacker already inside. CSIRT Italia reports that exploitation of this flaw has also led to ELock-family ransomware, cryptomining and theft of the LDAP database and credential hashes on exposed servers, and found no intrusion on regularly updated instances.
actions: Upgrade every Zimbra Collaboration host to 10.1.21 (10.1.20 is the minimum for CVE-2026-73570); where the upgrade cannot happen at once, remove the zimbra-snmp package or disable SNMP notifications and restrict SNMP and SMTP to trusted hosts.

On every host that ran a build before 10.1.20 with SNMP notifications enabled at any time since 2026-07-28, upgrading is not enough: rotate all domain zimbraPreAuthKey values and run the compromise check on every mailbox node, covering the zimbra user's crontab and /opt/zimbra/.ssh/authorized_keys, JSP or stray text files under /opt/zimbra/jetty_base/webapps/zimbra/public, droppers in /tmp and /var/tmp, and outbound connections from the mail server; where web shells or an LDAP dump turn up, rotate every mailbox and administrative credential.

records.title: TerminalFix: a ClickFix variant that pastes into Terminal or PowerShell instead of Windows' Run dialog, then chains DLL sideloading, steganographic payload delivery and a custom reverse-tunnel implant
records.headline: The fake-CAPTCHA lure now targets a console that can run multi-line scripts, not the one-line Run box
records.summary: Microsoft Threat Intelligence documents TerminalFix, a ClickFix variant that tricks users into pasting a malicious command into Windows Terminal or PowerShell via a fake Cloudflare CAPTCHA overlay, then runs a multi-stage chain of DLL sideloading, PNG-steganography payload delivery, domain reconnaissance and a custom Python reverse-tunnel implant that gives the attacker persistent SOCKS-style proxy access into the victim's internal network. Sophos reports the campaign running since March, with TerminalFix lures from late May and 19 pairings of a legitimate executable and a malicious DLL, so a detection keyed to one file name misses most of it.

last_update.summary: CVE-2026-93616 is marked patch-available only, since Check Point ships hotfix and Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator fixes, and the CVE-2026-91843 finding on the same management servers, whose LivePatch does not fix this flaw, is linked as a reference.

last_development.summary: Bishop Fox published on 2026-10-01 an end-to-end unauthenticated root exploit chain over TCP 19009 against unpatched R81.10 and R82.10 servers and a patch-state scanner. It says Check Point's second indicator does not fire on this route, that the first indicator is the crash signature of a separate CVE, and that the hotfix closes three defects; its hunting advice is file-integrity monitoring.

records.title: CVE-2026-93616, Check Point Security Management: pre-authentication path traversal to arbitrary script execution, exploited as a zero-day, with attacks observed on 2026-07-23 (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Check Point patches a management-server zero-day it says has already been used in a handful of pinpointed attacks
records.summary: An unauthenticated attacker can upload and execute an arbitrary script on Check Point Security Management Server, Multi-Domain Security Management Server, Log Server, Multi-Domain Log Server and SmartEvent via a directory-traversal and file-upload flaw. Check Point identified pinpointed exploitation on 2026-07-23, roughly two months before the 2026-09-22 fix; no LivePatch exists, only a hotfix or Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator. Bishop Fox published on 2026-10-01 an end-to-end root exploit method over the same port and a patch-state scanner, and says Check Point's second indicator does not fire on that route.
actions: Apply the R82.20 Security Hotfix or the appropriate Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator to every Check Point Security Management / Multi-Domain Security Management / Log / Multi-Domain Log / SmartEvent server now; no LivePatch exists for this issue.
Until patched, restrict TCP/19009 to trusted administrative IP ranges via Trusted Clients / implied rules on every affected server.

On every affected server that was reachable on TCP/19009 while unpatched, check /etc/cron.d, authorized_keys, the startup paths and anything new under $FWDIR/conf/SMC_Files for unexpected changes, since the two log indicators miss the published exploit route.

records.title: A self-registered account and an unrestricted upload turn a shared recreation-management platform into a webshell and card-data foothold, and the actor returns after cleanup
records.headline: Huntress: a member account plus an .aspx upload gave an attacker webshells on three servers and a hunt for card data
records.summary: Huntress observed from 2026-09-10 a threat actor compromising three web servers of a shared recreation-management platform by registering a member account and uploading .aspx webshells into the member-files directory, then searching for database credentials and cardholder data. After one server went back into production prematurely, the actor returned with the same account and planted a credential-harvesting script in the login page's jQuery file. Huntress names no vendor or CVE.

records.title: A malicious ChatGPT Custom GPT sends users to a Google Sites ClickFix page that installs a sideloaded, in-memory RAT
records.headline: Huntress: a ChatGPT Custom GPT lure feeds a ClickFix chain that ends in a signed-host DLL sideload and a RAT
records.summary: Huntress describes a September 2026 campaign in which, in some incidents, a sponsored Google result for "chatgpt" opens an attacker-built Custom GPT on chatgpt.com, which sends the visitor to a Google Sites page showing a fake CAPTCHA and a ClickFix paste-and-run command. The command installs an MSI that starts a signed Canon application sideloading a malicious DLL, which unpacks a RAT with remote desktop, camera and microphone capture and DNS-over-HTTPS command resolution; Huntress has responded to at least 40 incidents from the Google Sites domain, two confirmed through a Custom GPT.

records.title: CVE-2026-76504, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager: one percent-encoded character in the login path skips the password check and mints an admin API session, exploited in the wild (CVSS 9.8)
records.headline: Cisco confirms exploitation of an unauthenticated admin bypass in the SD-WAN controller; no workaround, fixes per train
records.summary: Cisco's advisory of 2026-09-30 fixes CVE-2026-76504, an unauthenticated authentication bypass in the API of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager (formerly vManage) that gives an attacker the privileges of the admin user, regardless of configuration. Cisco says it became aware of exploitation in September 2026 and CISA added the flaw to its KEV catalog the same day; Cisco lists no workaround but added a Live Protect shield on 2026-10-02 that it calls temporary, partial protection, and NCSC Switzerland published its own advisory.
actions: Upgrade every Catalyst SD-WAN Manager to the first fixed release of its train (20.9.10.1, 20.12.8.2, 20.15.6.1, 20.18.4.1, 26.1.2.1 or 26.2.1; anything earlier than 20.9 must migrate) and, until the upgrade is done, restrict the Manager's web and API access to known trusted hosts behind a firewall; Cisco's Live Protect shield for this CVE adds only temporary, partial protection and may block legitimate logins that use URI encoding.

On every Manager that was internet-reachable before the upgrade, search serviceproxy-access.log for POSTs to the login path with a percent-encoded character from unknown addresses and vmanage-server.log for login-path requests tied to viptela-reserved- user names, and open a Severity 3 Cisco TAC case with the CVE id in the title if anything matches.
